Each task operates on distinct but interrelated domains: temporal prediction, spatial localization, view generation, coordinate mapping, and semantic reasoning. These tasks are mathematically unified through shared data modalities and evaluation protocols, enabling cross-task generalization. BAA employs temporal convolutional networks to predict future ball events; PCBAS applies spatiotemporal attention to localize actions with player attribution; NVS synthesizes new views using 3D scene representations; SSS maps 2D image points to 3D pitch coordinates; and VQA uses multimodal transformers to answer questions about game states. Dualities emerge in how each task encodes temporal and spatial structure, with failure modes tied to occlusion, ambiguity, or domain shift. The framework supports retroactive analysis of model behavior through conformal prediction and Bayesian inference, ensuring robustness against adversarial inputs and data drift.
